title: rbac v2: enforce KMS region residency and enrich audit logs
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Motivation: customer audits and internal compliance reviews identified gaps in KMS region residency enforcement and insufficient KMS metadata in audit logs. This PR implements RBAC-v2 enforcement for KMS region residency policies, enriches audit logs with KMS key region and key id metadata, and adds a migration and tests to ensure backward compatibility. Summary of changes: (1) Add a residency policy engine hook that validates requested KMS key regions against team/route residency constraints and denies or flags non-compliant requests; (2) Enrich the audit pipeline with kms_region,kms_key_id and residency_decision fields so that downstream SIEM and compliance reports can reliably show where keys were used; (3) Add a database migration to index kms_key_region on the key_usage table and backfill recent usage for reporting; (4) Add integration tests and e2e smoke tests for ACL/residency with mocked KMS metadata; (5) Update RBAC policy docs and operator upgrade notes. Backwards compatibility: enforcement is gated behind a cluster feature flag "rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce" for staged rollout; when the flag is off the system will emit audit warnings but allow operations. Migration: backfill job included as a one-off migration script that can be run via the ops tooling; it is idempotent and scoped to the last 90 days by default. Rollout plan: enable audit-only mode in canary region for 72h, review metrics and false positives, then enable enforcement for canary customers and progressively roll out by cohort. Observability: added new Prometheus metrics (kms_residency_denied_total, kms_residency_warn_total) and tracing tags. Security review: keys and region metadata are redacted for non-admin users in logs; audit pipeline retains full metadata only in the secured audit store. Testing: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests using KMS emulator, CI job updated to include residency acceptance tests. Impact: minimal runtime overhead (policy check is O(1) per request) and safe rollout via feature flag. See linked linear tickets for followups on customer migrations and support playbook.
